chain.label: No requirement for ADS-B In traffic advisory systems with aural alerting in Part 135 passenger-carrying operations
chain.trigger: The FAA requires ADS-B Out only in certain airspace. There is currently no requirement for ADS-B In.

chain.label: FAA post-Capstone upgrade replaced the DHC-3's alerting-capable GDL 90 with a RANGR 978 lacking alerting, without mitigating the loss
chain.trigger: the FAA upgraded the ADS-B components with new components that did not maintain the existing alerting capability

chain.label: DHC-3 avionics could not place traffic in 'alert status', so the Chelton EFIS could not generate traffic alerts
chain.trigger: The RANGR 978 transceiver was not designed to send 'alert status' messages; therefore, the DHC-3 did not have the capability to generate aural or visual traffic alerts.

caused_by.evidence: the legacy traffic-alerting capability that was present on the DHC-3 was consequently lost

chain.label: Taquan Air used a checklist created for another operator with no GSL 71 item, and had no SMS to identify the hazard
chain.trigger: the checklist did not have an item about the GSL 71 control panel

chain.label: DHC-3's Garmin GSL 71 selector knob left in OFF since April 29, so the airplane broadcast no pressure altitude
chain.trigger: The Garmin GSL 71 control head selector knob was in the OFF position... the DHC-3 had not transmitted pressure altitude or a valid transponder code

caused_by.evidence: A procedural safeguard, such as a checklist item that addresses the position of the Garmin GSL 71 control head selector knob, can mitigate the hazard of the selector knob being inadvertently and indefinitely placed in the OFF position.

chain.label: ForeFlight treats traffic targets with no altitude data as distant and never alerts on them
chain.trigger: the manner in which the ForeFlight application currently handles missing altitude data from traffic targets precludes the application from providing visual and aural alerts concerning these targets

chain.label: Two air tour airplanes converged on the same scenic waterfall on intersecting tracks in a high-concentration air tour area
chain.trigger: both airplanes had been conducting sightseeing flights and were both converging on a scenic waterfall... while operating in a geographic area with a high concentration of air tour activity

chain.label: Neither airplane's cockpit traffic display produced a visual or aural alert as the conflict developed
chain.trigger: limitations in their alerting capabilities resulted in neither pilot being alerted to the impending collision

caused_by.evidence: the absence of a requirement for airborne traffic advisory systems with aural alerting among operators who carry passengers for hire
the alerting feature available on the Chelton EFIS could not be activated
The DHC-3 was not broadcasting pressure altitude because its GSL 71 control head was powered off; as a result, the ForeFlight application did not identify the DHC-3 as a collision threat
no visual or aural alert would have been generated because no altitude information about the DHC-3 would have been available

chain.label: DHC-2 pilot never visually acquired the DHC-3, which was obscured by cockpit structure, the right wing, and the front-seat passenger
chain.trigger: the DHC-2 pilot would not have had the opportunity to see the DHC-3 (which was above and behind his aircraft), by visually scanning the outside environment

caused_by.evidence: the DHC-3 approaching the DHC-2 from above and to the right, and the DHC-2 approaching the DHC-3 from below and to the left
the ForeFlight application did not identify the DHC-3 as a collision threat and did not initiate a corresponding alert

chain.label: DHC-3 pilot never visually acquired the DHC-2: hidden behind the left window post, tiny visual angle, no apparent motion, attention directed right toward the waterfall
chain.trigger: The DHC-2 would have likely remained hidden behind the DHC-3 window post until 0.5 second before the collision... he was looking to the right so that he could maneuver his airplane toward a waterfall

caused_by.evidence: the DHC-2 would have produced little apparent motion as the two airplanes converged at a relatively constant angle for about 3 minutes before the collision
If the DHC-3 CDTI had given the pilot an aural alert to notify him of the impending traffic conflict, the pilot may have reacted differently and avoided the collision.

chain.label: The two airplanes collided in midair at 3,350 ft, 7.4 nm northeast of Ketchikan Harbor Seaplane Base
chain.trigger: The airplanes collided at 1221:14 at an altitude of 3,350 ft, 7.4 nm northeast of 5KE.

caused_by.evidence: the inherent limitations of the see-and-avoid concept, which prevented the two pilots from seeing the other airplane before the collision
even if the DHC-3 pilot had seen the DHC-2, he would not have had enough time to avoid the collision

chain.label: DHC-2 broke up in flight; right wing cut apart and fuselage fractured, all five occupants ejected
chain.trigger: The DHC-2 was fractured into multiple pieces... The fuselage of the DHC-2 broke up during the midair collision, and all five occupants were ejected

caused_by.evidence: a series of mechanical cuts were noted on the aft portion of the wing from the right aileron inboard to the wing root

chain.label: DHC-2 wreckage impacted the water and terrain northeast of Mahoney Lake over a 3,000-ft debris field
chain.trigger: impacted the water and terrain northeast of Mahoney Lake

caused_by.evidence: The debris field was about 3,000 ft long and about 800 ft wide and located mostly on land.

chain.label: Damaged DHC-3 descended and impacted George Inlet, pitching over and sinking
chain.trigger: The DHC-3 began descending and completed a 180° turn before impacting George Inlet at 1222:15

caused_by.evidence: the DHC-3 experienced a brief upset in vertical load factor and soon after entered a right bank, reaching an attitude about 50° right wing down

chain.label: Six fatalities (DHC-2 pilot and four passengers, one DHC-3 passenger), nine serious and one minor injury
chain.trigger: The DHC-2 pilot and four passengers sustained fatal injuries. The DHC-3 pilot sustained minor injuries, nine passengers sustained serious injuries, and one passenger sustained fatal injuries.

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for all five was blunt force trauma
an autopsy determined her cause of death was 'blunt impacts of head, trunk, and extremities.' A contributing condition to her death was drowning.
